question: Is the wrong-character residue decidable at glyph-crop resolution?
answer: Yes. 81 percent of resolved disagreements adjudicate to the gold form under a blind, balanced forced choice, with a 3.6 percent control break rate, lifting real patched sequence recall from 0.8468 to 0.9402 mean with every one of 24 pages improving.

observations.ordering_pages_decomposition: GL-1054-1-12 (0.2492 to 0.9088, +217) and GL-1054-1-13 (0.3455 to 0.8121, +154) gain partly by re-asserting per-location identity where full-page reading misordered panels; excluding both, the remaining 22 pages still move 0.8968 to 0.9474.
observations.gold_noise_class_named: 169 resolved disagreements sided WITH the output against gold, dominated by the same variant families in reverse (巳/已 13, 圎/圓 9, 𫝹/念 7, 爲/為 6, 縁/緣 6): blind crop evidence that MTHv2 annotators themselves sometimes normalized. These are gold-correction candidates under the gold protocol, not model errors.
observations.cost_note: single resumable pass; the 5 smoke instances are included in the same results file and total, ceiling 4.0

decision_detail: The information the full-page reader loses IS on the page at crop resolution: a blind per-glyph forced choice recovers 81 percent of the wrong class and breaks almost nothing. This validates glyph adjudication as the next production instrument. It is not yet a production capability: this measurement used gold label boxes for localization and gold-vs-output pairs for the choice set. Production wiring needs (1) detector-box localization (RF-DETR boxes exist per column), (2) a trigger set built without gold - second-reader disagreements plus a variant-watchlist - and (3) an open choice set or watchlist-pair choice. That is the next bounded experiment (toolbelt v5).
next_permitted_action: Design toolbelt v5: production-legal glyph adjudication (detector-box localization, gold-free trigger set), then the paired MTHv2 run under both lenses.
